description.p: Bard keeps everything you copy, from any application, in one searchable history: text, links, colours, images and files. Your pinned and most recent items sit in three slots that one shortcut puts back on the clipboard from anywhere. Copies a password manager marks as private are never kept.

Hold a key and talk, and a speech model running on your own computer turns what you said into text and puts it on the clipboard. Audio never leaves the machine. Or open a page and sketch with pens, arrows, shapes and text, then copy it as a picture or save it as SVG.
Bard only ever works through the clipboard you already use. It never types into another application, has no account and no telemetry, and goes online only to download a speech model you ask for.

description.p: The Linux packages now state Bard's MIT licence correctly, and Bard carries the metadata Linux software centres show: its description, screenshots and release notes.
Bard is now free and open source. This version adds a badge that confirms each copy, shortcuts you change and check in one place, and windows that tuck away when you click elsewhere.
Dictation no longer loses parts of a recording on desktops that deliver audio in large blocks, and a copy Bard cannot read is retried and reported instead of skipped.
